**Finding: Compliant (no redline proposed).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **Section 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the natural location for a usage-verification right — contains only substantive covenants (no copying, no reverse engineering, no sublicensing) with no inspection, reporting or system-access mechanism.
- **Section 20 (General Matters)** covers only time-of-essence and notices; **Section 14 (Confidentiality)** is mutual and contains no access-for-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *examine*, *records*, *premises*, *monitor* and *compliance* surface nothing binding on us. The single examination right in the document (escrow materials, p0114) runs in **our** favour, letting Sparkling retain independent experts to test Garman's deposited materials.
- The only termination-related obligation is a self-certification of deletion (p0118), which is not an audit right.

Since the playbook position is a *cap* on vendor audits, their complete absence is better than the preferred position. Proposing frequency/notice/cost limits would gratuitously create an audit right Garman does not have, so we should leave this alone. If Garman later requests verification language in negotiation, we would hold to the preferred position: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.
